judged_text: Scope drift: the loadUsers rewrite (a) silently removes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user Prisma select and (b) wraps the whole loader in a catch that converts every non-HttpError failure into a 500 'Unable to load users' — neither is traceable to the destinationCalendar intent. Dynamic collective bookings lose user.organization on every loaded user, so any downstream consumer of user.organization.slug (org-branded handling on the booking path) now sees undefined; additionally, transient Prisma errors that previously surfaced with their real message now return a generic 500, changing API error behavior on an untouched requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show scope drift in `handleNewBooking.ts`’s `loadUsers` rewrite: in the `prisma.user.findMany({ select: { ... } })` branch, the prior `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` selection is removed (it’s deleted in the new `select` block), so dynamically loaded users will no longer include `user.organization.slug`. The new `try/catch` also changes error behavior by converting any non-`HttpError` / non-`PrismaClientKnownRequestError` into a generic `HttpError` 500 (`"Unable to load users"`). However, the diff alone doesn’t prove that downstream code on this path actually requires `user.organization.slug` (i.e., it’s a plausible break but not directly demonstrated here), so it’s best classified as a significant review concern rather than a definitively verifiable bug from the diff alone.
